newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bubble hangover deflates Daikyo Inc profits.
newsitem.headline: Bubble hangover deflates Daikyo Inc profits.

text.p: Daikyo Inc said on Friday its earnings dropped sharply last year due to continuing fallout from the collapse of Japan's "bubble" economy, but it expects a recent condominium boom to help it in the future.
"Our profits fell in 1996/97, largely because of the disposal of inventories," a spokesman for the major condominium builder said.
Daikyo said its parent current profit in the year to March 31 fell 29 percent year-on-year to 5.16 billion yen ($44.4 million).
An appraisal loss on its securities holdings due to generally weak Japanese stock markets and the financial support Daikyo gave to units helped push down the profits, he said.
Daikyo cut its total dividend for 1996/97 to 7.50 yen, down from 10 yen in 1995/96.
Daikyo forecast a parent current profit of four billion yen ($34.4 million) this year and said it plans a further cut in its total dividend to five yen.

Daikyo and other Japanese real estate firms have suffered from the collapse of property prices after the late-1980s "bubble" era of inflated asset prices. They are currently disposing of assets at lower prices than they initially set.
"Unlike some property firms, we do not dispose of inventories at one time, so the sale of inventories will continue pressuring our earnings for some more years," the spokesman said.
He did not say when Daikyo's earnings would start a fully fledged recovery but was not pessimistic.
"Although we expect our current profit to drop further in 1997/98 because of disposal of inventories, we see our sales and net profit rising this business year."

Demand for condominiums had been robust mainly due to low interest rates, he said. The bursting of the property bubble lowered property prices and has made it easier for Japanese to buy houses and condominiums, he said.
"We enjoyed a high level of contracts last year and they will help push up our profit in the current business year," he said. ($1=116 yen)
